assagai: a light spear thrown by hand, used in southern African warfare
assagais: plural of assagai, a light hand-thrown spear
digging-stick: a pointed wooden stick used to dig up the ground
mantle: a loose sleeveless cloak worn over the shoulders
kraal: an enclosure of thorn fencing for keeping cattle and livestock
cattle-fold: an enclosure where cattle are kept safe at night
milksack: a bag made of animal skin, used for storing and churning milk
milk-basket: a basket used for carrying or holding milk
ladle: a large deep spoon used for serving liquids
calabash: a hard-shelled gourd dried and used as a bowl or container
kerries: knobkerries, short wooden clubs with a heavy knobbed head
eland: a large African antelope with spiralled horns
ock-a-doodle-doo: the crowing sound a rooster makes at dawn
cannibals: people who eat the flesh of other human beings
witch-finder: a person who claims to identify and expose witches
sacrifices: offerings of animals or goods made to spirits or gods
ancestors: forefathers and forebears who lived long before the present
malevolent: wishing harm or evil upon other people
invulnerable: unable to be wounded, harmed, or defeated in battle
furnace: an enclosed fire chamber used to melt or smelt metal ore
smelt: to heat ore in order to extract metal from it
retinue: a group of attendants who travel with an important person
commonalty: the ordinary people of a community, as opposed to its rulers
chieftainship: the rank, office, or authority of a tribal chief
councillors: advisers who counsel a chief or ruler on decisions
petty: minor or lesser in rank, importance, or authority
traditionary: passed down by word of mouth through generations
folklore: traditional stories, beliefs, and customs handed down orally
wares: goods or articles offered for sale or trade
implements: tools or instruments used for a particular task
clicks: speech sounds made by pressing and releasing the tongue
abstract: naming a quality, idea, or feeling rather than a physical thing
iguana: a large tropical lizard with a row of spines along its back
baboons: large monkeys with doglike muzzles living in Africa
superstition: a belief in magic or luck not based on reason or evidence
narrators: people who tell stories, especially traditional tales
haste: great speed or urgency in doing something
famine: a widespread severe shortage of food causing hunger and death
cunning: clever at deceiving or achieving one's aims by trickery
boulder: a very large rounded rock lying on the ground
species: a group of living things of one particular kind
charms: objects believed to hold magical power to protect or harm
medicines: traditional remedies and magical preparations used by healers
